implementation_notes: DRF ships the pattern: CursorPagination presents an opaque cursor query parameter (cursor_query_param) and requires a unique, unchanging ordering - ordering = '-created' by default or an OrderingFilter with a restricted field list - and returns only forward/reverse links, guaranteeing that a client never sees the same item twice while rows are inserted, at the cost of random access. Outside DRF the design is the template: encode the last (created_at, id) pair as a token and query WHERE (created_at, id) < (:ts, :id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT :n + 1, which is the classical hand-written form with SQLAlchemy or a raw cursor.
pitfalls: DRF's "position plus offset" cursor copes with near-unique values, but ordering by a mutable or non-indexed field (its own docs use name) still produces buggy pages - verification should assert no duplicates and no skipped rows under concurrent inserts.

A float ordering field accumulates precision errors that make the cursor land on the wrong side of a row; use decimals (or an integer tiebreaker) and remember that CursorPagination cannot jump to an arbitrary page.
